chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Shah narrated that Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hussein said: Abu Yazid Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Khalidy narrated that Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimi narrated from his father that Anas ibn Muhammad Abu Malik narrated from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

He said in his will to him: 'O Ali! There is no banquet (walimah) except in five cases: a wedding, childbirth, circumcision, buying a house, and returning from Mecca.' The wedding is marriage, the childbirth is the confinement with the baby, the circumcision is the cutting of the foreskin, the buying of the house is the banquet for purchasing a home, and the returning from Mecca is the banquet for one who comes back from Mecca. The compiler of this book, may God be pleased with him, said: The food to which people are invited when building or buying a house is called 'al-Wakirah', and 'al-Wakar' is derived from it. The food prepared for the one returning from travel is called 'al-Naqi'ah'. 'Al-Rakaz' means booty, as if he means that preparing food for the return from Mecca is a booty for its host from the abundant reward. And from this is the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'Fasting in winter is the cool booty.'

key_terms.النَّقِيعَة: Banquet held for welcoming someone returning from travel
key_terms.الْوَكِيرَة: Banquet held for buying or building a house
key_terms.رَكَّاز: Return from Mecca; literally means booty or treasure
key_terms.وَلِيمَة: Banquet or feast, specifically a celebratory meal

ai.seo_question: What are the five occasions for holding a walimah (banquet) in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this tradition in *Al-Khisal*, emphasizing that the Prophet’s instruction to Ali ibn Abi Talib restricts formal banquets to five specific occasions: marriage, childbirth, circumcision, purchasing a home, and returning from Mecca. The compiler elucidates that these feasts are viewed as acts of worship yielding immense reward, metaphorically termed 'booty' (rakaz), thereby elevating social gatherings to spiritual merits.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-93 Muhammad ibn Ali ibn ash-Shah narrated that Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hussein quoted on the authority of Abu Yazid Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Khalidy, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimy, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas ibn Muhammad Abu Malik, on the authority of his father, on the authorityof Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his grandfather (MGB) that Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB) said, “O Ali! Banquets should only be served in five situations: wedding parties, birth of babies, circumcision, purchase of houses, and returning from Mecca (after performing the Hajj).”

The compiler of the book - may God be pleased with him - said, “One form of banquet which is referred to as Vakira is for buying or building a new house. Another form of banquet which is referred to as Naqia is for returning from a journey. In fact, the word Rekaz means booties. It refers to the banquet served upon returning home from the Hajj pilgrimage in Mecca, since the pilgrim considers it to have an extra reward for him. In a similar statement, the Prophet (MGB) said ‘fasting in the month of Ramazan is similar to booties.’
